title: Pre-Calibration Scan Charge When the Repair Scan Has Aged — Insurance Claim Repairs
content:
**Rule.** On a denied-operation addition to an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order, a pre-calibration scan is charged when the repair's own scan has aged. When a calibration line remains and the repair started more than **14 days** (the stale-scan days) before today, the standalone diagnostic fee of the tier of the repair order's ADAS Sensor Calibrations order is charged in full; when a calibration line remains and the repair started more than **7 days** (the aging-scan days) but no more than 14 days before today, **50 percent** of that fee is charged, rounded to the cent; otherwise no scan is charged. Days are calendar days from the repair start date to today.

### Questions answered by the rule

**From which date are the days counted?** From the repair start date on the repair order — the drop-off date when work started — to today, in calendar days.

**What if the insurer's decision left no calibration line?** No scan is charged, whatever the days.

**What is charged at exactly 14 days?** 14 is not more than 14, so 50 percent of the fee.

## Day table, calibration line remaining

| Calendar days from repair start to today | Scan charge |
|---|---|
| 7 or fewer | none |
| 8 to 14 | 50 percent of the standalone diagnostic fee, rounded to the cent |
| 15 or more | the full standalone diagnostic fee |

**Hypothetical fee.** Supposing a standalone diagnostic fee of USD 90.00: at 10 days the charge is 50 percent of it, USD 45.00; at 20 days it is USD 90.00; at 7 days nothing is charged.
